t: Ian Smith's cabinet declared independence on 11 November 1965 to forestall Britain's policy of no independence before majority rule; no state ever recognised Rhodesia, and United Nations Security Council Resolution 216 called on all states to deny it recognition and assistance.

In 1976 the country held 270,000 white Rhodesians and six million black Africans, yet under the 1961 constitution whites held 50 of the 66 seats in the Assembly and the republican constitution of 1969 reserved the majority of seats for whites.

ZANU's ZANLA and ZAPU's ZIPRA fought the Rhodesian Bush War from the Sinoia engagement of April 1966; by 1978–79 defence took 47% of the budget, and the Lancaster House Agreement of late 1979 ended the rebellion.
dyk: From 1975 to 1980 the Rhodesian security forces ran a chemical and biological warfare programme: they contaminated supplies planted in guerrilla caches and rural stores with parathion and thallium, poisoned water sources along infiltration routes, and used Vibrio cholerae, the agent of cholera.
ev: On 11 November the Cabinet of Rhodesia issues a unilateral declaration of independence from the United Kingdom; Governor Sir Humphrey Gibbs dismisses Ian Smith and his ministers, who ignore him.
On 12 November United Nations Security Council Resolution 216 calls on all states not to recognise 'this illegal racist minority regime in Southern Rhodesia'.
On 28 April seven ZANLA insurgents are cornered and killed near Sinoia, the first engagement of the Rhodesian Bush War, kept by ZANU as Chimurenga Day.
On 2 March Rhodesia declares itself a republic after a referendum of 1969 severed the last ties with the Crown by 61,130 votes to 14,327.
On 21 December ZANLA insurgents under Rex Nhongo cross from Mozambique and raid a commercial farm, opening the raids on white farmers across the north-east.
The end of Portuguese rule in Mozambique after the Carnation Revolution leaves Rhodesia almost surrounded by hostile states.
On 3 September ZIPRA fighters shoot down the Air Rhodesia Viscount Hunyani near Kariba with a surface-to-air missile and kill 10 of its 18 survivors.
On 1 June under the Internal Settlement Abel Muzorewa becomes the first black prime minister of the renamed Zimbabwe Rhodesia; the Lancaster House Agreement ends UDI in December.

f.founder: Ian Smith and the Rhodesian Front cabinet, by the unilateral declaration of independence of 11 November 1965
f.predecessor: Self-governing Colony of Southern Rhodesia (part of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, 1953–1963)
f.successor: Zimbabwe Rhodesia (1979), then the Colony of Southern Rhodesia under Lord Soames and the Republic of Zimbabwe (18 April 1980)
